userStories.title: Define tool annotation types and HTTP method classification
userStories.description: Create TypeScript types for MCP 2025 tool annotations (readOnlyHint, destructiveHint, idempotentHint, openWorldHint) and a classifyHttpMethod() function that maps OpenAPI operation metadata to annotation objects. GET → readOnlyHint:true + idempotentHint:true, DELETE → destructiveHint:true + idempotentHint:true, POST/PUT → default no hints. All tools get openWorldHint:false. The function takes the OpenAPI operation's HTTP method and operationId as inputs and returns a ToolAnnotations object.
acceptanceCriteria: ToolAnnotations type exported with fields: readOnlyHint?, destructiveHint?, idempotentHint?, openWorldHint? (all boolean | undefined)
classifyHttpMethod('get', operationId) returns { readOnlyHint: true, idempotentHint: true, openWorldHint: false }
classifyHttpMethod('delete', operationId) returns { destructiveHint: true, idempotentHint: true, openWorldHint: false }
classifyHttpMethod('post', operationId) and classifyHttpMethod('put', operationId) return { openWorldHint: false } with no other hints set

userStories.title: Idempotent pattern detection for POST/PUT operations
userStories.description: Extend classifyHttpMethod() with a known-idempotent pattern list for POST/PUT operationIds. Operations whose operationId contains 'approve', 'reject', 'cancel', 'acknowledge', 'read', 'mark' should additionally get idempotentHint:true. The pattern list is a const array of substrings checked via operationId.toLowerCase().includes(). This allows Claude Code to skip confirmation for idempotent mutations like spec approval.
acceptanceCriteria: IDEMPOTENT_PATTERNS constant array contains at least: 'approve', 'reject', 'cancel', 'acknowledge', 'read', 'mark'
classifyHttpMethod('post', 'rorca_approve_spec') returns { idempotentHint: true, openWorldHint: false }
classifyHttpMethod('put', 'rorca_mark_done') returns { idempotentHint: true, openWorldHint: false }
classifyHttpMethod('post', 'rorca_generate_spec') returns { openWorldHint: false } with NO idempotentHint (generate is not idempotent)

DELETE-sourced tools have destructiveHint:true visible in tools/list response

userStories.title: Define structured error response types and HTTP-to-MCP error code map
userStories.description: Create a McpStructuredError type with fields: ok (false literal), code (string enum: NOT_FOUND, VALIDATION_ERROR, AUTH_ERROR, FORBIDDEN, CONFLICT, UNPROCESSABLE, RATE_LIMITED, SERVER_ERROR), error (string), suggestion (string), tool (string), timestamp (ISO string). Create a httpStatusToMcpError() mapping function that takes an HTTP status code and returns the corresponding error code. Create a SUGGESTION_MAP constant mapping each error code to a default contextual suggestion string (e.g. NOT_FOUND → 'Check workspaceId with rorca_get_workspaces', RATE_LIMITED → 'Wait and retry in 60 seconds').
acceptanceCriteria: McpStructuredError type exported with all 6 required fields typed correctly
httpStatusToMcpError(400) returns 'VALIDATION_ERROR', httpStatusToMcpError(404) returns 'NOT_FOUND', httpStatusToMcpError(429) returns 'RATE_LIMITED'
httpStatusToMcpError(500) and httpStatusToMcpError(502) both return 'SERVER_ERROR'
SUGGESTION_MAP has entries for all 8 error codes with actionable suggestion strings
SUGGESTION_MAP['NOT_FOUND'] mentions rorca_get_workspaces, SUGGESTION_MAP['VALIDATION_ERROR'] mentions checking required parameters

userStories.title: Build mkStructuredError() factory and integrate into executeApiCall()
userStories.description: Create mkStructuredError(toolName: string, httpStatus: number, errorMessage: string): McpStructuredError that assembles the full structured error object using httpStatusToMcpError() for the code, SUGGESTION_MAP for the suggestion, ISO timestamp, and the provided tool name and error message. Then modify the executeApiCall() error handling path in mcp-http.ts: when the internal HTTP call returns a non-2xx status, construct a McpStructuredError via mkStructuredError() and return it as the MCP tool result with isError:true. The content array should contain a single text item with JSON.stringify(structuredError, null, 2) so both human-readable and machine-parseable.
acceptanceCriteria: mkStructuredError('rorca_get_workspaces', 404, 'Workspace not found') returns object with ok:false, code:'NOT_FOUND', error:'Workspace not found', suggestion containing 'rorca_get_workspaces', tool:'rorca_get_workspaces', timestamp as valid ISO string
executeApiCall() error path returns MCP result with isError:true flag
MCP error result content[0].text is valid JSON matching McpStructuredError schema
A 429 rate limit response returns code:'RATE_LIMITED' with the retry suggestion

userStories.title: Enhanced error suggestions with tool-specific context
userStories.description: Extend mkStructuredError() to accept an optional overrideSuggestion parameter. In executeApiCall(), detect specific tool+status combinations and provide targeted suggestions: any spec tool returning 404 → 'Spec not found — list specs with rorca_list_specs'; any workspace tool returning 404 → 'Workspace not found — list workspaces with rorca_get_workspaces'; pipeline trigger returning 409 → 'A run is already active — check status with rorca_pipeline_status or pass queue:true'; memory tools returning 400 → 'workspaceId is required — get it from rorca_get_workspaces'. Fall back to SUGGESTION_MAP default if no specific match.
acceptanceCriteria: Tool name containing 'spec' + status 404 returns suggestion mentioning rorca_list_specs
Tool name containing 'workspace' + status 404 returns suggestion mentioning rorca_get_workspaces
rorca_pipeline_trigger + status 409 returns suggestion mentioning queue:true
Unknown tool + status 404 falls back to SUGGESTION_MAP default suggestion for NOT_FOUND

contextUsed.text:
=== GLOBAL STANDARDS (L1) ===
principles:
  typescript:
    strict_mode: true
    target: ES2022
    no_any: "Avoid `any` — use `unknown` with type guards or explicit generics"
    async_first: "All DB calls, LLM calls, and I/O are async — always await"

  error_handling:
    pattern: "AppError class hierarchy with immutable HTTP status codes"
    subclasses: [ValidationError 400, AuthError 401, ForbiddenError 403, NotFoundError 404, ConflictError 409, UnprocessableError 422]
    serialization: "{ error: string, code?: string, details?: Record<string, unknown> }"
    rule: "Throw from route handlers; centralized errorHandler middleware catches and serializes"

  database:
    driver: "pg Pool (async, connection pooling)"
    helpers: "query<T>() returns T[], queryOne<T>() returns T|undefined, execute() returns { rowCount }"
    placeholders: "$1, $2, ... (numbered, NOT positional ?)"
    transactions: "transaction<T>(fn) wraps in BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK"
    migrations: "SQL files in pg-migrations/, timestamp prefix YYYYMMDDHHMMSS for new files, tracked in schema_migrations"
    slow_query_logging: "Queries > 500ms logged with sanitized params"

  validation:
    library: zod
    pattern: "Middleware factories — validateBody(schema), validateQuery(schema), validateParams(schema)"
    method: "safeParse (not .parse() which throws)"
    response: "{ error: firstIssueMessage, details: zodError.issues }"

  llm:
    return_type: "ChatResult { text: string, usage: { inputTokens, outputTokens } }"
    rule: "Always use .text accessor — never treat ChatResult as a string"
    providers: "Multi-provider routing via model registry — claude-cli, anthropic, openai-compat, openrouter"

  api_design:
    documentation: "JSDoc @swagger annotations on every route → auto-generated OpenAPI spec"
    pagination: "{ items: T[], total: number, hasMore: boolean, cursor?: string }"
    response_shape: "Success: res.json(data). Error: { error, code, details } via AppError"
    middleware_chain: "validateBody(schema) → authRequired → async handler"
    security_headers: "helmet (CSP, HSTS, X-Frame-Options, noSniff, referrerPolicy)"
    caching: "Cache-Control: no-store on all responses, etag: false"

  testing:
    backend: "Jest with ts-jest, serial (maxWorkers: 1), 30s timeout, PG_POOL_SIZE=1"
    frontend: "Vitest with jsdom, globals: true"
    rule: "Always clean up DB pool connections in afterAll()"

  code_style:
    no_over_engineering: "Only make changes that are directly requested or clearly necessary"
    no_premature_abstraction: "Three similar lines > premature helper function"
    minimal_containers: "Don't add docstrings, comments, or type annotations to code you didn't change"
    security_first: "Never commit .env files, API keys, or secrets. Use vault for sensitive values."

=== PROJECT CONTEXT (L3) ===
name: rorca
type: web-app
purpose: AI spec orchestration platform that converts plain-English briefs into structured user story specs and autonomously executes them story-by-story via isolated agent subprocesses (claude, opencode, or codex)

stack:
  - React 18
  - TypeScript 5.7 (strict)
  - Vite 5
  - Tailwind CSS 3
  - xterm.js (@xterm/xterm)
  - react-router-dom 7
  - framer-motion
  - recharts
  - Express.js
  - PostgreSQL 16 (pg pool, pgvector, Apache AGE)
  - pg-boss (job queue)
  - Node.js >= 20
  - tsx (TypeScript runner)
  - Jest (backend tests)
  - Vitest (frontend tests)
  - Playwright (E2E)

key_modules:
  - src/panels/ — 5 primary UI panels (Specs, Runs, Analytics, Direction, Settings)
  - src/components/ — shared UI (Sidebar, RunTerminal, CommandPalette, slide-overs)
  - src/contexts/ — WorkspaceContext, AuthContext, ThemeContext, ToastContext
  - backend/src/routes/ — 32 Express route files
  - backend/src/lib/ — core services (sse-hub, direction-stack, llm-client, execution-engine, context-router, workspace-echolocation, rate-limiter, scheduler)
  - backend/src/worker.ts — pg-boss worker process (pipeline job consumer)
  - backend/src/lib/execution-engine.ts — sole execution engine for all agent types
  - backend/src/db/ — PostgreSQL pool, migration runner, 70+ migrations
  - backend/src/mcp/ — MCP stdio server (24 tools)
  - forge/ — spec JSON files, run-loop.sh bash fallback, self-register script

constraints:
  - Migrations must use timestamp format YYYYMMDDHHMMSS for new files (sequential 001-079 already exist)
  - Worker process must be running for pipeline triggers to execute
  - AGE search_path must be restored after every graph query
  - Auth middleware is globally disabled (intentional, local tool)
  - CLAUDE_BIN full path required for child process spawning (NVM PATH not inherited)
  - spec id is always the filename slug, never the human title

deployment_target: local (self-hosted, npm run dev) or Docker Compose

ports:
  frontend: 5210
  backend: 3030
  finops_sim: 5200

integrations:
  - claude CLI (claude --print)
  - opencode CLI (opencode run)
  - codex CLI (codex --approval-mode auto-edit)
  - GitHub OAuth + webhooks
  - Linear (post-launch)
  - Vercel (post-launch)
  - Slack (post-launch)
  - Stripe billing

=== SPEC BRIEF (L4) ===
Improve the Rorca MCP HTTP transport with three state-of-the-art enhancements:

1. **Tool Annotations** — Auto-annotate all OpenAPI-generated MCP tools in mcp-http.ts with MCP 2025 spec annotations:
   - GET operations → readOnlyHint: true, idempotentHint: true
   - DELETE operations → destructiveHint: true, idempotentHint: true
   - POST/PUT with known-idempotent patterns (approve, reject, cancel) → idempotentHint: true
   - All tools → openWorldHint: false (Rorca tools operate on known workspace data)
   This allows Claude Code to auto-approve read-only tool calls without prompting the user.

2. **Structured Error Responses** — Replace raw string error messages in the HTTP MCP handler with structured JSON errors matching the stdio server's mkError() pattern:
   - { ok: false, code: string (e.g. NOT_FOUND, VALIDATION_ERROR, CONFLICT), error: string, suggestion: string, tool: string, timestamp: string }
   - Map HTTP status codes to semantic error codes (400→VALIDATION_ERROR, 401→AUTH_ERROR, 403→FORBIDDEN, 404→NOT_FOUND, 409→CONFLICT, 422→UNPROCESSABLE, 429→RATE_LIMITED, 5xx→SERVER_ERROR)
   - Add contextual suggestions per error code (e.g. NOT_FOUND → "Check workspaceId with rorca_get_workspaces")
   - isError: true flag preserved for MCP protocol compliance

3. **MCP Resources** — Register workspace context files as MCP Resources on the HTTP transport:
   - rorca://workspace/{workspaceId}/direction — synthesized direction stack (L1-L5)
   - rorca://workspace/{workspaceId}/memory — recent memories (last 20, titles only)
   - rorca://workspace/{workspaceId}/agents — AGENTS.md content if exists
   - rorca://workspace/{workspaceId}/health — workspace health report
   - Implement resources/list and resources/read handlers in mcp-http.ts
   - Resources are read-only (no write capability)
   - Return appropriate mimeType (text/plain for markdown, application/json for structured data)

All changes are in backend/src/lib/mcp-http.ts only (plus any needed route additions). No changes to stdio server.ts. No new dependencies — uses existing @modelcontextprotocol/sdk@1.26.0 and existing API routes.
